verdict.rationale: Stagehand's extract() takes an instruction plus an output shape and validates the result against that shape before returning it, so the data comes back typed rather than as raw text. The cache docs confirm extract() is a first-class primitive. Missing for 10: the docs quoted here never name Zod or Pydantic as the schema format, and there is no independent or hands-on corroboration of schema validation.

support.subject: As a developer, I can extract typed, schema-validated data (Zod/Pydantic-style) from pages the agent visits, not just raw text

citations.quote: extract() grabs structured data from a webpage. Every call takes an instruction and an output shape
Stagehand validates the result against that shape before returning it, so what you get back is already typed.
